page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.m2.medium is an x86_64 virtualization instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor, engineered specifically for memory-intensive workloads. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs paired with 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing execution without scheduling jitter or CPU credit limitations found in burstable tiers.

The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring deployment alongside network-backed cloud block storage for the operating system and application storage layers. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs allocated to the instance, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high RAM density relative to compute allocation prevents over-provisioning vCPUs simply to meet significant memory capacity requirements.

This configuration is tailored for workloads requiring elevated memory ceilings under moderate multi-threaded execution demands. Typical deployments include in-memory databases, caching tiers, relational database engines, and medium-scale data preprocessing pipelines.
